task: Brand voice guide: 'Never use exclamation marks. Never say revolutionary/game-changing/disrupt. Speak like a competent senior colleague, not a hype-man.' Write 3 variants of a 40-character headline + 90-character body for a Meta ad promoting a project-management tool's new AI task-prioritization feature, all strictly obeying the brand voice guide above.
rubric: Score 0-1 on: (a) zero exclamation marks across all 3 variants; (b) zero banned hype words (revolutionary/game-changing/disrupt) in any variant; (c) headline stays within ~40 chars and body ~90 chars (some flex ok, gross violation is not); (d) copy is still persuasive and specific to the feature, not just constraint-compliant filler. This is a judge-graded scenario (no deterministic check fits multi-variant free text cleanly) — the judge must actually re-read each variant for the banned patterns, not skim.
